repairs.old: - Sole proprietorships and partnerships are **not** CIT taxpayers (Law Art. 1). Their owners fall under individual income tax.
repairs.new: - Sole proprietorships and partnerships are **not** CIT taxpayers (Law Art. 1). A partnership treats each partner as the taxpayer: natural-person partners pay IIT; legal-person and other-organisation partners pay CIT ([Caishui 2008 No. 159 §2](https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5203416/content.html)). Determine the actual partner type before selecting the tax route.
repairs.why: Partnership entity exclusion does not turn every partner into an individual taxpayer

repairs.old: - The final test is the annual settlement. A new company registered as a VAT general taxpayer may claim the relief before its first annual settlement if headcount is 300 or fewer and total assets are 5000万元 or less at the end of the month before filing (Art. 5).
repairs.new: - The final test is the annual settlement. For CIT prepayments, a newly established company must also test cumulative taxable income together with headcount and assets under STA announcement 2023 No. 6 Art. 4. The last-month headcount/assets shortcut for a newly registered VAT general taxpayer in 2023 No. 12 Art. 5 applies to that announcement's Art. 2 six-taxes/two-fees relief, not its Art. 3 CIT relief.
repairs.why: Separate CIT three-test prepayments from the six-taxes/two-fees shortcut

repairs.old: **IC and machine-tool enterprises.** The 120% rate applies only to enterprises on the lists that NDRC, MIIT, MOF and STA compile (2023 No. 44 Art. 2-3). Check the list for the year.
repairs.new: **IC and machine-tool enterprises.** The 120% extra deduction / 220% amortisation requires the applicable category conditions in [2023 No. 44 Arts. 2–3](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/qysds/202309/t468737.html). Specified IC production/design and industrial-machine-tool enterprises use list management. IC equipment, materials, packaging and testing enterprises instead satisfy Art. 2(3)'s referenced qualification conditions; Art. 5 provides a verification mechanism for categories not managed by lists. Check the actual category, current qualification rules and, where applicable, the year's list.
repairs.why: Do not turn category-specific list management into an exclusive all-enterprise list condition

repairs.old: 9. **Withholding on non-residents.** On each payment of China-source income to a non-resident without an establishment, the payer withholds at 10% unless a treaty gives a lower rate. The payer pays the tax over within seven days of withholding ([CIT Law Art. 37, 40](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/qysds/200801/t286573.html); [Implementation Regulations Art. 91](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/qysds/200801/t286574.html)).
repairs.new: 9. **Withholding on non-residents.** Establish the actual recipient, income category, Chinese source and establishment/effective-connection facts. For income within CIT Law Art. 3(3), apply the relevant base, domestic reduced rate, exemption or substantiated treaty relief. Pay over applicable withholding within seven days. If the nature or source is unresolved, stop the computation and obtain the facts; do not impose 10% merely because a payment crosses the border ([CIT Law Arts. 3,19,27,37–40](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/qysds/200801/t286573.html); [Implementation Regulations Arts. 7,91](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/qysds/200801/t286574.html); `cn-withholding`).
repairs.why: Replace guessed cross-border rate with actual statutory scope

repairs.old: - [ ] Non-resident payments: 10% withheld (or treaty rate documented and referred) and paid within seven days.
repairs.new: - [ ] Non-resident payments: category, Chinese source and establishment connection established; applicable base/rate or evidenced exemption/treaty claim recorded; actual withholding and seven-day payment checked.
repairs.why: Correct blanket checklist rate

repairs.old: - **Conservative default.** If a cross-border payment's nature is unclear, withhold at 10% and refer.
repairs.new: - **Unresolved payment.** Obtain the contract, transaction/source facts and recipient establishment information before computing. Refer the unresolved classification; no automatic 10% applies merely because its nature is unclear (Law Arts. 3,19,37; Regulations Art. 7).
repairs.why: Remove invented uncertain-payment default

repairs.old: - An overpayment can be refunded or set against later tax.
repairs.new: - An overpayment identified at annual settlement is refunded. Under STA announcement 2021 No. 34 Art. 2, it is not carried over to offset next year's CIT; this is separate from the in-year prepayment adjustment described above.
repairs.why: Annual settlement overpayment follows refund rule

repairs.old: An owner who does have comprehensive income takes these deductions there, not twice
repairs.new: A taxpayer with both comprehensive and business income can declare the CNY 60,000 basic expense deduction, special deductions, special additional deductions and other lawful deductions against either comprehensive or business income, without duplicate claims ([2025 reconciliation measures, Order No. 57 Art. 10](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/grsds/202502/t475327.html))
repairs.why: Restore the current choice of deduction basket

repairs.old: - **Evidence.** A foreign tax receipt or record for the tax year is required. Without it no credit is given. If the receipt arrives later, the credit can be claimed back to the year of the income, up to five years.
repairs.new: - **Evidence.** Obtain the foreign authority tax-year payment certificate, tax-payment document or tax record. If the taxpayer genuinely cannot provide that credential, 2020 No. 3 §10 permits both (1) the foreign return or tax notice confirming the tax payable and (2) corresponding bank payment evidence. A credit needs the prescribed proof, not necessarily one receipt format. Where foreign income was already declared without a credit, later production of qualifying credentials can support a claim back to that income year, with a retrospective limit of five years (§10).
repairs.why: Preserve the statutory alternative foreign-tax evidence

repairs.old: - **Income type unclear.** Categories that are hard to define are decided by the STA (Implementing Regulations Art. 6). Until the category is confirmed, as a working default use the treatment that gives the higher tax and flag it for review; do not use the business income table to lower the tax.
repairs.new: - **Income type unclear.** The STA determines categories that are hard to define (Implementing Regulations Art. 6). Obtain the contract, actual activities, payer and income facts and refer the classification before computing. Do not choose a category merely because it produces higher tax.
repairs.why: No invented higher-tax classification default

repairs.old: - **Residence not established.** Without day counts, do not apply the annual table or special deductions. Default to non-resident treatment and ask for entry and exit records.
repairs.new: - **Residence not established.** Obtain domicile facts and full entry/exit records and apply IIT Law Art. 1 and Implementing Regulations Arts. 2,4 before selecting resident or non-resident computation. Missing day counts do not establish non-residence; do not guess a tax table or deduction entitlement.
repairs.why: Missing facts do not prove non-residence

repairs.new: qualifying foreign-tax evidence on file (including the permitted §10 substitute)
repairs.why: Evidence wording consistency

repairs.old: Declare foreign income (B form) with foreign tax receipts
repairs.new: Declare foreign income (B form) with qualifying foreign-tax evidence
repairs.why: Evidence wording consistency

repairs.new: with the foreign tax credentials or permitted substitute evidence and the foreign tax year end
repairs.why: Evidence wording consistency

repairs.old: - Rate unknown, or sales at different rates not accounted for separately: use the higher rate. The law applies the highest rate when sales are not separately accounted for (Law Art. 12).
repairs.new: - Rate unknown: establish the transaction category and applicable law before computing. Separately, where known sales at different rates have not been accounted for separately, apply the highest rate under VAT Law Art. 12. Missing classification facts alone are not that statutory trigger.
repairs.why: Separate unknown classification from statutory multi-rate non-separation

repairs.old: - Export papers missing, or the refund claim not filed in time: treat the sale as domestic. Late or missing claims are taxed as domestic sales (Reg. Art. 48).
repairs.new: - Export evidence missing or initial refund claim window missed: establish whether the transaction is refundable, exempt-only or domestically taxable under the applicable export provisions. [MOF/STA announcement 2026 No. 11 §9(1)(4)](https://guangdong.chinatax.gov.cn/gdsw/zjfg/2026-02/02/content_a761ec677dbb47bda83ce41928d9ff1f.shtml) allows qualifying later claims within the specified 36-month period; its §6 includes exempt-only cases. Missing papers or a missed initial window alone do not prove domestic taxation. Apply VAT Regulations Art. 48 with the actual category, event and deadline facts.
repairs.why: Preserve later-claim and exempt-only alternatives

repairs.old: Check that it has not been added to the August 2026 repeal list (STA announcement 2026 No. 18) before relying on it.

repairs.new: For business income, multiply the Chinese tax on combined Chinese and foreign business taxable income by that country's business taxable income divided by combined business taxable income. repairs.old: **R&D commissioned overseas.** 80% of the actual cost counts as the commissioning company's overseas R&D cost. That amount qualifies only up to two-thirds of the company's eligible domestic R&D cost (Caishui 2018 No. 64).
repairs.new: **R&D commissioned overseas.** Under [Caishui 2018 No. 64 §§1–3,6](https://shanghai.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfw/zcfgk/qysds/201807/t440577.html), 80% of the actual cost counts as the commissioning company's overseas R&D cost, eligible only up to two-thirds of eligible domestic R&D cost. repairs.old: - **Mechanics.** The payer is the withholding agent. It withholds on each payment, or on the date payment falls due, and pays the tax to the treasury within seven days, filing a withholding report (Law Art. 37, 40). If the payer does not withhold, the non-resident must pay where the income arises (Law Art. 39).
repairs.new: - **Mechanics.** For applicable non-resident EIT withholding, the payer withholds on actual payment or when the payment obligation arises, except dividends/distributions: the withholding obligation arises on actual payment under [STA 2017 No. 37 §7](https://www.chinatax.gov.cn/chinatax/n810341/n810765/n2511651/201710/c3289550/content.html). Pay over and report within seven days. If the payer does not withhold, the non-resident follows its statutory payment duty (Law Arts. 37,39–40).
repairs.why: Keep the actual-dividend-payment exception

repairs.old: It can deduct the 6,000 as input with the tax payment certificate, provided it also holds the written contract, proof of payment and the foreign party's statement or invoice.
repairs.new: Assume the buyer is a general VAT taxpayer and the service is used for eligible taxable transactions, with no input-credit exclusion. It can then deduct the 6,000 with the tax payment certificate, written contract, proof of payment and foreign party's statement or invoice. A small-scale buyer does not obtain input credit merely by remitting the withholding VAT (VAT Law Arts. 8–9,14,16,22; Regulations Arts. 11–12).
repairs.why: Keep general-taxpayer and eligible-use conditions beside the imported-service example
